name: Unakoti Heritage Site (Rock Carvings)
description: Ancient Shaivite rock-cut sculptures site dating to 7th-9th centuries CE in Unakoti district. Features colossal 30-foot bas-relief of Unakotiswara Kal Bhairava (Shiva) with attendant figures, Ganesha images, Nandi bulls and hundreds of other carvings amid forested hills and streams. UNESCO tentative World Heritage list (2022); also known as Subrai Khung in Kokborok.
facts: UNESCO World Heritage tentative list since 2022
Central Shiva head ~30 ft high with 10 ft headdress

name: Kailashahar
description: District headquarters of Unakoti and municipal town on the Manu River near the Bangladesh border. Historic gateway and base for Unakoti site, with temples, tea gardens and administrative importance. Elevation around 30 m.
facts: Nearest airport Agartala; rail via Kumarghat/Dharmanagar

name: Khowrabil Lake (Khaowra Bil)
description: Historic lake near Kailashahar (also called Rajar Dighi), site of annual traditional water festival with boat races in October-November. Associated with ancient palace history and nearby Chaturdas Devata Mandir; attracts local visitors.
facts: Annual water festival with boat race
Mentioned in historical accounts as large tank

name: Chaturdas Devata Mandir (Rangauti)
description: Temple dedicated to the fourteen deities (Chaturdasa Devata) of Tripuri tradition, located near Rangauti/Khowrabil area of Kailashahar. Linked to historical capital narratives in Rajmala; important local pilgrimage site.
facts: Dedicated to 14 deities of Tripuri pantheon
Historical association with Indra Manikya era
Official tourist place of Unakoti district

name: Unakoti Eco Park
description: Nature park near the Unakoti heritage site developed for visitors to rest amid greenery after exploring the rock carvings. Suitable for short walks and picnics in the forested setting.

name: Jampui Hills
description: Highest hill range in Tripura (average ~1,000 m, peaks to 930 m), part of the Lushai Hills in North Tripura. Known as the Eternal Hills of Spring or Orchid Paradise of India for its temperate climate, dense greenery, orange orchards, and over 50 orchid species including rare Vanda coerulea. Mizo-influenced villages, viewpoints over Bangladesh and Mizoram, and eco-tourism base.

name: Betlingchhip Peak (Thaidawr / Shibraikhong)
description: Highest peak in Tripura at 930 m on the Jampui Hills ridge in North Tripura district. Offers panoramic views of surrounding hills, Chittagong Hill Tracts of Bangladesh, and Mizoram forests. Accessible by short hike/scramble from nearby villages; features a watchtower built by Tourism Department.
facts: Highest point in Tripura at 930 m
Also known as Thaidawr or Shibraikhong
Panoramic views of Bangladesh and Mizoram

name: Vanghmun Village
description: Remote hilltop village at the highest part of Jampui Hills in North Tripura, widely regarded as the cleanest village in Tripura. Home to Mizo community with neat wooden houses, hedges, orchid gardens, and strict cleanliness maintained by village council. Base for Betlingchhip Peak and eco-tourism stays including Eden Tourist Lodge.
facts: HQ of Jampui Hills R.D. Block
Gateway to Betlingchhip and orange orchards

name: Shilchhara Buddha Waterfall
description: Hidden gem waterfall near Pecharthal town in North Tripura, cascading amid lush forest. Offers a serene, tranquil setting for nature walks; lesser-known compared to major sites and ideal for quiet visits. Access involves local transport from Pecharthal.
facts: Official tourist place of the district

name: Rowa Wildlife Sanctuary
description: Compact wildlife sanctuary (0.858 km²) established in 1988 near Panisagar in North Tripura. Features deciduous, semi-evergreen and mixed moist deciduous forests with bamboo. Supports barking deer, wild boar, pig-tailed macaque, birds, and reptiles; suitable for short nature walks and birdwatching despite anthropogenic pressure.
facts: Home to macaques, deer, birds and reptiles
Official tourist attraction of the district

name: Kalibari Temple (Dharmanagar)
description: Revered Hindu temple dedicated to Goddess Kali in Dharmanagar town, North Tripura. Serves as a spiritual and cultural centerpiece for local devotees, with festivals and community gatherings. Located in the district headquarters area.
facts: Official tourist place listed by district

name: Dharmanagar
description: District headquarters and second-largest town in Tripura, located on the Juri River near the Bangladesh border in North Tripura. Important commercial and administrative center, gateway for Jampui Hills circuit, with markets, Kali temple, and connectivity by road and rail.
facts: On Juri River near Bangladesh border
Base for Jampui Hills and northern circuit
